runner: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-26.04, 4 vCPUs (AMD EPYC 7763, 2 cores x 2 threads), QEMU machine pc-q35-10.0

failures.phase: idle precision, every AP halted (spec 06 §4 revision of 11 November 2026)
failures.observation: Every segment counted exactly 1000 IRQ0 and lasted 0.34-1.54% longer than the PIT period on the PIT-calibrated TSC; the median is 1.05%. This is the lost-edge pattern described in CLOCK-INVESTIGATION.md (overdue PIT edges merge into one pending PIC IRR bit). The other 49 soaks and every other case passed the same idle check.
No FAIL, PANIC or progress marker after GO. The IPC phase prints nothing until it completes, so the transcript cannot distinguish slow progress from a hang.

failures.failure: aggregate rejects the two failures above; the final gate is skipped

pass only because of the 650 s diagnostic watchdog; exceeds 180 s

local_reproduction.refuted_hypothesis: Giving the ordinary canary PAUSE hint on one pass in 64 instead of every pass (less MTTCG BQL churn) made the 2-CPU run slower: 431.9 s against 326.7 s. The change was reverted and is not part of any commit.
local_reproduction.interpretation: The 10 000 rounds complete with the unchanged oracle, zero wait timeouts and no FAIL marker. Under multi-thread TCG the IPC phase runs at about one round per scheduler tick on 4 host CPUs and about 0.37 round per tick on 2; the dominant cost is an endpoint preempted by its CPU's tick and requeued behind three CPU-bound canaries. Wall time therefore scales with host CPU capacity, while single-thread TCG stays near 100 s. The 180 s watchdog was derived from 71.8 s on a faster host (ADR-081 R3-5 addendum) and is below the completion time on the hosted 4-vCPU runner class.
